DrChen.description: conversing about a conversation between Dr. Chen and Dr. Wang discussing the recent increase in respiratory cases in Dr. Chen’s clinic, a scheduling mix-up involving a respiratory patient mistakenly seen in Dr. Wang’s dermatology clinic, and the implementation of a new triage and referral protocol to prevent such errors. @ <persona> DrWang
chat: Hi Dr. Wang—just catching a quick break between patients. I saw you handling that dermatology case efficiently. We’ve been swamped in the respiratory clinic lately with this uptick in dry cough and low-grade fever cases. How’s your day going?

Hi Dr. Chen. My day’s been steady—mostly contact dermatitis cases from new detergents or skincare products. Just had a scheduling mix-up this morning; someone with fever and cough showed up in my clinic by mistake. Glad they’re now with you. How many respiratory cases are you seeing daily?

We’re seeing about 30 to 35 respiratory cases a day now—mostly mild, but we’ve started triaging more strictly. Anyone with fever over 38°C or oxygen saturation below 94% comes straight to me, while milder cases get rapid flu and RSV tests at triage first. It’s helped streamline things a bit. That mix-up you mentioned is exactly why we updated the referral protocol this morning with Nurse Li.

Good to hear the new triage protocol’s in place—should cut down on cross-clinic mix-ups. I’ll make sure my front desk references it. If I see another respiratory case by mistake, I’ll send them straight over with a note.
